rv.q: There have been quite a few Cabarets over the years – in addition, of course, to the film – but this is the most compelling I have ever seen. All too often, it has amounted to little more than a mournful tale about the rise of Nazi Germany with, rather clumsily grafted on, a few big, brassy numbers like The Money Song and Maybe This Time.
Despite some startlingly athletic moves it is deliberately slaggy, crotch-y, imprecisely seedy stuff. Which I quite liked, in context.
Had Norris dared more from the outset, however, this could have been a rare piece of musical theatre, challenging as well as entertaining.
It's a dark, jagged and ultimately harrowing production that brings some welcome shade to a West End overrun with the lightness of 'enforced standing ovation' jukebox fare.

cn.t: Critics praise this dark, harrowing revival for its powerful final act and compelling staging that strips away cabaret glamour to reveal Nazi-era brutality. Will Young's Emcee debut earns strong marks, though some find the production uneven.
